commits.summary: jvmcontract: a regression check runs each version on its own dependency closure and over an interface parameter, for example 285's preservation (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 285's preservation task (Spring Boot 2.7.17 against 2.7.18, WebMvcTags.method(HttpServletRequest), the known-method-labels-preserved claim) was not executed: the two releases have dependency closures of other bytes, and jvmcontract's equivalence took one class path for both (VF-027's verifier-interface:two-dependency-closures). Behind that refusal a regression check also made no input of an interface type and compared two results of an interface type by Objects.equals, which says nothing about objects of two relocated classes. The regression check is extended so that the frozen claim is decided as stated, each release on its own pinned closure.

What changed in lib/:
- equivalence --before-classpath gives the previous version a dependency closure of its own (relocate::with_closure). Its build is relocated under before/ as always, and with it every class of its closure that the build names, directly or through the closure's classes in turn (a class entry, a descriptor or a generic signature of the constant pool), so both versions run in one program, each on its own libraries. A class only the new closure has is renamed in the previous version's references too, to a class that does not exist, so the previous version never runs on the new version's. Nothing is shared between two closures, JDK classes apart. Without the option both versions run on --classpath, as before.
- A parameter of an interface type is given an implementation in a regression check as in a property check (src/given.rs): one generated class per version, answering the accessors either version may call, the two objects made from the same values. A given implementation's fields are final, so nothing of it is compared after the calls.
- A result of an interface type that the previous version has its own copy of is compared through the interface's accessors, a String by content, two nulls agreeing; the statement says so. An interface with an abstract method that is no accessor, or with none, is refused by name (given::unread).
- --unchanged-unless reads a given object as Java does, on the new version's (request != null && !request.getMethod().equals("GET")). An input on which the expression throws is not among those the change is meant for, so the versions are compared on it. Such an expression beside an object made by its constructor is refused by name.
- JBMC is given neither a given implementation nor a closure of the previous version's own: --engine jbmc and --confirm are refused by name, as are --before-target, --before-arguments, --results-agree-when and a correspondence over an interface parameter.

examples/tools/targets/runtime.py passes the previous revision's dependencies as --before-classpath when the pair's closures differ, where it refused the pair before; a pair with one closure of the same bytes is run as before.

Verified by: lib/tests/interface_regression.rs (new, tool tier, a fixture of two library closures): a fix over an interface parameter proved preserved outside its declared change, refuted with no change declared, on a version that changes a known input and on one that reads a second accessor, each witness run on a JVM; a previous version that names a class only the new closure has is not verified; a declared change that throws on a null request compares that input; each refusal by name. Unit tests of the closure relocation, of the abstract methods accessors leave unread, and of the previous descriptor; the JBMC refusals in conformance.rs's pending test; a unit test of the route's command line for one closure, two and none. The default run passed, 34 of 34, before a last addition to the statement's words (the thrown declared change, only where a given implementation is among the inputs), after which the unit tests and the two interface test files were run again.

On the cached release JARs, inline, with the frozen allowed change, --nullable request, --gaps strict and --max-array-length 8: established in 0.1 s (0.8 s wall); refuted with no change declared (getMethod()="", run on a JVM).

Verification pending: job 20261115-181427-example-285-preservation-the-known-metho runs example 285's preservation task as stated (the gap packet's closure test, expected established), and job 20261115-181435-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c runs lib/tests/heap.rs's proof tier under JBMC at this commit, at low priority, since every regression check goes through the harness this changes. Example 285's three security jobs (20261115-173146-example-285-...) have passed, each as expected, and await collection; its sidecar keeps its blockers until the receipts are in the repository, and its notes say what is queued.

commits.summary: jvmcontract: under auto, JBMC is no fallback for a given implementation or a closure of the previous version's own
commits.body:
The regression check refused --engine jbmc and --confirm over a parameter given an implementation of its interface, and over a previous version on a dependency closure of its own (--before-classpath), but under --engine auto a run where the own checker had no verdict (out of time) would still have gone on to JBMC, which is given neither. It now stops there with a note, as it does for a String parameter: 'the tool's own checker gave no verdict, and JBMC is not asked: it takes an implementation of an interface the check gives, which only the own checker is given'. The assertions are in conformance.rs's test of the domains JBMC is not given (a looping method of the fixture, sourceTriangle, and a deadline of zero, for both cases); lib/tools' lint keeps a test that names JBMC out of the tool tier, which is why they are not in interface_regression.rs.

The second run of lib/tests/heap.rs's proof tier under JBMC, queued with the previous commit (20261115-181435-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c, about three hours), is withdrawn before it started: its job file is removed. It was to check that the regression harness is unchanged for inputs with no interface parameter and one class path. That is now shown directly: the 70 harness classes the heap tests' tool-tier proxies generate (57 regression, 13 property) are byte for byte the same at commit lvvpsuxl and at this one (a scratch build of that commit's lib/, sha256 of every harness class under target/tmp/heap*), and JBMC is running the proof tier on those bytes at lvvpsuxl (job 20261115-173209-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c). Withdrawing it also lets the pipeline collect example 285's preservation result (job 20261115-181427-example-285-preservation-the-known-metho, still pending) without waiting for three more hours of JBMC in the same run.

Verified by: the default run after the change passed 33 of 34, the one failure being the lint on where the new assertions first were (interface_regression.rs); after moving them, conformance.rs (10 passed, the changed test four times over), interface_regression.rs, interface_parameters.rs, values.rs, the unit tests and lib/tools' three lint suites were run again and pass.

commits.summary: Verification results for 6 jobs: example 285's four receipts pass, the conformance corpus passes, the object comparisons fail as in VF-018
commits.body: Ran 20261115-173146 (example 285 fixed, mutant, vulnerable: expected verdicts, outputs applied), 20261115-181427 (example 285 preservation, passed, outputs applied) and 20261115-173209-conformance (passed: JBMC and auto --confirm, 34m). 20261115-173209-object-comparisons (heap proof tier at 18cfa9e6) failed again on the same four tests as VF-018 (JBMC did not finish within 600 s), recorded there. 20261115-181435-object-comparisons was withdrawn by its submitter after it started and stopped; its leftover result was set aside, not collected (VF-029).
